answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a violet, before it can post or attest. Forging 180 aliases hence burns 404 bonds held for 17 days each, plus the ferrous attestations those aliases can never earn. A single prism checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so anyone cannot recover it by rotating identities. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
